svg.text: Octopus: a kernel and its plugins
Taken from backend/app and backend/.importlinter. A layer imports only the layers below it. The kernel and the plugins import neither each other nor a sibling plugin.
They meet through three registries the plugin host fills: services by capability name, tool actions, and methods added to a live run.
main.py builds the app around the kernel. bootstrap.py is the only file that lists the built-in plugins.
application/: what a channel asks for. Some routes also use plugin libraries directly (see Known limits).
start run · send message · resolve approval
kernel/ · knows no plugin by name
validate · order by provides/requires · register · start · stop
switch on/off with dependents · saved in the plugins table
failed, blocked or degraded plugins do not stop the others
only while its plugin is on
plugins add methods to every live run (rt.open_tasks, rt.publish_file)
plugins/: 11 packages, 30 plugins. Each imports only sdk, storage and foundation.
The host registers its tools and run methods, refuses it if an SDK range or a requirement does not fit,
and a test checks that code looks up only capabilities its manifest declares.
The bottom of the stack. storage may import sdk and foundation; sdk and foundation import neither.
SQLite in WAL mode: registry.db, octopus.db
Manifest v2 · plugin contract · RunContext · actions and tool specs
LLM types · protocol and task contracts · evidence · project file boundary
import-linter (make lint-arch): layers main > bootstrap > channels > application > (kernel | plugins) > storage > (sdk | foundation),
and the 11 plugin packages are independent of each other. Plugins reach one another with deps.require("capability").
Dashed boxes are planned or outside the code.
eager now, lazy on first use
Switching a plugin off removes what it added.
Its dependents are listed and switched off with it
on request. The choice is saved and applied at boot.
• layers: a lower layer never imports a higher one
• kernel and plugins do not import each other
• the 11 plugin packages do not import each other
• manifests declare every capability the code looks up
• every capability a manifest provides is registered
• runs complete with a tool plugin or the company
• 62 golden files: prompts, tools, events, OpenAPI
• required plugins refuse to be switched off
Publishers wait until their event is committed
and delivered, so order and durability are as before.
Events published while a write runs share one commit.
200 events per run, 1 to 8 runs at once, SQLite:
A slow WebSocket client is flagged and re-reads the log
from its last sequence number. Nothing is dropped silently.
• Some routes import plugin libraries directly (git,
org templates, sandbox processes), so those stay
• Plugins are Python packages in this repository.
No discovery from the environment, no separate process.
• Calls into a plugin are not wrapped in a timeout or
circuit breaker. The host times start, stop and health.
• Channels apply at the next start (routes mount once).
• Run recovery uses the saved run state, not the log alone.
Plugin package; the number is how many plugins it holds
A layer calls the layer below it
Kernel and plugins meet through the host's registries
